title: Five Boston Shops for Outdoor Winter Gear

content: An array of Cotopaxi’s offerings. For the Well-Dressed Wanderer Kühl Kühl built its reputation on clothing that performs outside and looks sharp indoors, too. The new Boston store stocks men’s and women’s hiking and travel pants along with flannels, fleeces, sweaters, and outerwear. The earthy palette and streamlined silhouettes make this a strong stop for anyone who expects the same wardrobe to cover a morning hike and evening reservations at Contessa . 343 Newbury St., Boston, kuhl.com . For the Backpack Devotee Fjällräven The rainbow of boxy Kånken backpacks may grab your attention first, but Fjällräven ventures well beyond its best-known accessory. The Swedish brand specializes in durable, unfussy gear made for spending serious time outside: waxable jackets and trousers, insulated parkas, trekking packs, hats, and cold-weather layers. The aesthetic is unmistakably Scandinavian—practical, understated, and largely immune to trends. 342 Newbury St., Boston; 63 Church St., Cambridge; fjallraven.com . A base layer set from Stio. A base layer set from Stio. For the Powder Chaser Stio Jackson Hole–born Stio captures mountain-town style without leaning too heavily on ski-bum clichés. At its Seaport Mountain Studio, shoppers will find technical ski and snowboard shells, insulated jackets, base layers, fleeces, and après-ready knits for men, women, and kids. Its clean silhouettes and nature-inspired colors give the collection everyday appeal, while a curated selection of footwear, gloves, and other gear covers the accessories when the weekend forecast calls for snow. 49 Northern Ave., Boston, stio.com . A Norrøna jacket. For the Serious Summit Seeker Norrøna This Norwegian label has spent nearly a century developing gear for unforgiving terrain—and its Boston store carries the full collection. Expect highly technical jackets, bibs, pants, and packs engineered for skiing, mountaineering, hiking, mountain biking, and trail running. Its streamlined designs and vibrant color blocking are striking, but performance is always at the forefront. 349 Newbury St., Boston, norrona.com . For the Everyday Explorer Cotopaxi Catering to travelers, day hikers, and casual adventurers who want practical but vibrant gear, Cotopaxi’s best-known offerings include suitcase-style Allpa travel packs and one-of-a-kind Del Día bags made from leftover fabric, alongside colorful fleeces, puffers, windbreakers, and accessories. The pieces are built for movement but easy to fold into everyday life—ideal for anyone whose adventures are as likely to involve an airport as a trail. 201 Newbury St., Boston, cotopaxi.com .
